quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2026 results (CFO Brice Hill): revenue of $7 billion was in the upper end of the guidance range and down 2% year-over-year; non-GAAP gross margin grew 20 basis points year-over-year to 49.1%; non-GAAP operating profit declined 4% year-over-year to $2.1 billion; non-GAAP EPS of $2.38 was at the top of the guidance range and flat year-over-year. Revenue in China declined 7% year-over-year and represented 27% of combined semi equipment and AGS sales and 30% of overall sales. Semiconductor Systems revenue exceeded expectations and included record DRAM revenue, but declined 8% year-over-year to $5.14 billion, with non-GAAP gross margin up 100 basis points to more than 54% on value-based pricing and manufacturing cost improvements; Applied Global Services delivered record revenue of $1.56 billion, up 15% year-over-year. Cash from operations was $1.69 billion and free cash flow $1 billion (elevated capital investment for the EPIC R&D center and expanded systems manufacturing capacity); $702 million was distributed to shareholders. GAAP results include a $252.5 million accrual for an export controls compliance matter resolved through a settlement with the U.S. Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security. From this quarter the 200-millimeter systems business moved from Applied Global Services to Semiconductor Systems.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $7 billion (down 2% year-over-year); non-GAAP gross margin 49.1%; non-GAAP EPS $2.38; Semiconductor Systems $5.14 billion; Applied Global Services $1.56 billion; China 27% of semi equipment and AGS sales

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 FY2026 guidance: company revenue of $7.65 billion, plus or minus $500 million, up around 9% sequentially; non-GAAP EPS of $2.64, plus or minus $0.20; Semiconductor Systems revenue of around $5.8 billion, AGS revenue of about $1.6 billion and Other revenue of around $250 million; non-GAAP gross margin to increase to approximately 49.3%; non-GAAP operating expenses of around $1.415 billion (approximately 6% sequential growth, funding growth projects including early EPIC-related projects and accelerated R&D co-development with customers and partners, with spending to grow more slowly than revenue); non-GAAP tax rate of around 11%. CFO expects gross margin improvement to be modest and very slow through the year: faster Semiconductor Systems growth is a tailwind, while a flattish China and a receding mix of smaller customers is a headwind. Semiconductor Systems gross margin is approximately 54% and expected to keep improving as the portfolio shifts to more valuable products.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $7.65 billion, plus or minus $500 million (up around 9% sequentially); non-GAAP EPS $2.64; Semiconductor Systems around $5.8 billion; AGS about $1.6 billion; non-GAAP gross margin approximately 49.3%

quarterly_data.signal: CY2026 outlook: Applied expects to grow its semiconductor equipment business more than 20% this calendar year, with demand weighted to the second half and availability of customer cleanroom space the key factor pacing investment; largest customers are giving longer-term visibility and strong growth momentum is expected to carry into 2027 (CEO: '27 is shaping up to be another strong year). CEO believes global semiconductor industry revenues can potentially reach $1 trillion in 2026, several years earlier than prior predictions. Leading-edge foundry/logic, DRAM including HBM, and advanced packaging are expected to be the fastest-growing WFE segments in '26, '27 and the next several years, where Applied says it holds strong #1 process equipment positions. NAND is forecast for modest growth and to remain less than 10% of WFE; ICAPS WFE is now seen approximately flat year-on-year both globally and in China (last quarter Applied expected China and ICAPS WFE to be down a little on capacity digestion), with the ICAPS market growing mid- to high single digits longer term. Asked by an analyst whether the earlier ~15% WFE-intensity framing still holds, the CEO said WFE intensity has grown to around 15%, but that Applied's longer-term composition model now differs from the earlier 1/3 leading-edge foundry/logic, 1/3 ICAPS, 1/3 memory split because end-market growth rates have diverged - "it's time for a new growth framework" - with leading-edge foundry/logic and DRAM becoming significantly larger than ICAPS and other memory.
quarterly_data.figure: semiconductor equipment business to grow more than 20% in CY2026; industry revenues potentially $1 trillion in 2026; NAND less than 10% of WFE

quarterly_data.signal: Supply and capacity: CFO said leading-edge foundry/logic and DRAM capacity is essentially full and prices have increased, semiconductor factory utilization is rising across all device types, and Applied is tracking higher planned capex from cloud service providers. This year's shipments are metered by cleanroom in leading edge and DRAM - customers found more space to add DRAM and leading-logic capacity than planned a quarter ago but have exhausted most of it; a number of DRAM and leading-logic factories are scheduled to come online in '27, the count of new factory projects Applied tracks keeps rising each quarter, and Applied expects to "go into next year still in a constrained position." Applied has nearly doubled its system manufacturing capacity over the past several years and still has prepositioned space to scale much higher; it increased inventory by nearly $500 million year-over-year for rising build plans (inventory days approximately 153, not expected to rise much) and is giving its approximately 2,000 suppliers longer visibility and specific bills of material. CEO said customers now give significantly longer-term visibility with specific configurations because supply chain and service-engineer training take time.
quarterly_data.figure: inventory up nearly $500 million year-over-year; approximately 2,000 suppliers; inventory days approximately 153

quarterly_data.signal: Leading-edge logic: customers are adding capacity at FinFET nodes while ramping gate-all-around nodes, which grow Applied's available market considerably and give multiple points of share gain. CEO said Applied is #1 and on track to capture more than 50% of its served market in gate-all-around and wiring, including backside power, and is #1 in deposition, conductor etch and packaging. Applied plans to launch more than a dozen new products in 2026, including 3 for advanced logic and DRAM announced the week of the call: the Viva radical treatment system (angstrom-level engineering of nanosheet surfaces for faster gate-all-around transistors), Sym3 Z Magnum (newest Sym3 etch variant for critical etch steps in gate-all-around transistors and advanced DRAM) and the Spectral ALD system (selective deposition of monocrystalline moly, reducing contact resistance in advanced logic devices by up to 15%). Applied is leading the transition from ALD tungsten to ALD moly in logic contact formation, while copper PVD steps keep growing and remain an order of magnitude larger than ALD moly.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 50% of served market in gate-all-around and wiring; more than a dozen new products in 2026; contact resistance reduced by up to 15%

quarterly_data.signal: Process diagnostics and control: Applied expects revenue from its cold field emission (CFE) eBeam technology to double this calendar year to more than $1 billion, making it one of the fastest-growing businesses in 2026; CEO cites the highest resolution and 10x faster imaging, says new material-characterization products will be announced, and has very high confidence the growth continues at a high rate in '27. Management declined to give a specific size for the PDC business.
quarterly_data.figure: CFE eBeam revenues to double this calendar year to more than $1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Data center share of wafer starts (CFO): Applied previously said more than 20% of leading-edge wafer starts were directed to data center; this year data center passes PCs in consumption of leading-edge wafer starts, and Applied moved up its forecast so that data center surpasses smartphones in 2029. CFO's rough model: traditional data center (racks, file servers) growing between 10% and 20% and AI-related components growing between 30% and 40%, giving something north of 20% overall. CEO, citing discussions with his largest customers' CEOs and R&D leaders (who talk about extremely high compound annual growth rates), said he thinks AI data center demand is a significant wave that will last over a longer period, and expects '27 to also be a very strong year.
quarterly_data.figure: previously more than 20% of leading-edge wafer starts directed to data center; data center to surpass smartphones in 2029; AI-related components growing between 30% and 40%

quarterly_data.signal: Applied Global Services: record Q1 revenue grew 15% year-over-year on the recast basis (200-millimeter systems moved to Semiconductor Systems), with non-GAAP gross margin up 210 basis points and operating margin up 320 basis points; the Q2 guide implies approximately over 12%, almost 13% year-over-year AGS growth. CFO expects AGS to grow at low double digits or better going forward on a 55,000 tool installed base that grows 5-plus percent every year; the business is all recurring revenue, with 2/3 under contract, an average contract of 2.9 years and a 90% renewal rate, and its cash profitability can cover the dividend. More than 30,000 chambers are connected to AIx servers for AI-powered monitoring, diagnostics and analytics, delivering 30% faster response times, and all major distribution centers are now automated with AI-enabled robotic systems. CEO sees an opportunity for AGS to grow faster as customers ramp gate-all-around, backside power and complex memory architectures.
quarterly_data.figure: 55,000 tool installed base; 2/3 under contract; average contract 2.9 years; 90% renewal rate; more than 30,000 chambers connected to AIx

players.product: deposition/etch/CMP tools and TSV via formation equipment

quarterly_data.signal: DRAM/HBM: Semiconductor Systems Q1 revenue included record DRAM revenue. Customers are aggressively adding capacity at 6F-squared nodes while developing next-generation DRAM architectures, and CFO says most DRAM investments being made are greenfield. HBM has larger die sizes and requires 3 to 4x more wafer starts per delivered bit than standard DRAM - going from HBM3 to HBM4 takes that from 3x to 4x - and the number of dies in HBM stacks is increasing from 12 today to 16 and then 20 or more, further growing demand for wafer starts and advanced packaging. Applied says it is #1 in standard DRAM, HBM DRAM and HBM packaging (leader in materials deposition for wiring and patterning, with rapid growth in conductor etch and eBeam), calls DRAM its strongest business after significant share gains over the last decade, and has very high confidence it will keep growing share in 6F-squared and 4F-squared.
quarterly_data.figure: HBM requires 3 to 4x more wafer starts per delivered bit (HBM3 to HBM4 goes from 3x to 4x); HBM stacks from 12 today to 16 and then 20 or more dies

connects_to.relationship: process tools for DRAM and TSV

contracts.signal: CEO Gary Dickerson: "This week, we also announced our first EPIC co-development agreement with Samsung Electronics." EPIC gives chip makers significantly earlier access to Applied's R&D portfolio for faster transfer of next-generation technologies into high-volume manufacturing, and gives Applied better multi-node visibility and a better ability to be designed in with its products and advanced service technologies; EPIC comes online later this year. Announced the same week as 3 new products for advanced logic and DRAM; the call does not say which Samsung business (memory or foundry) the agreement covers.

players.product: high-aspect-ratio etch/deposition & ALD tools for 3D NAND channel holes

quarterly_data.signal: NAND: Applied forecasts modest growth in NAND equipment demand in 2026, growing slower than AI-driven segments and remaining less than 10% of wafer fab equipment spending. CFO says NAND hasn't increased wafer output in several years because bit density gains at every node let the industry meet demand with the starts in place, so the NAND business is mostly conversions and upgrades, where Applied participates less from a share perspective; Applied is shipping product but expects most of it to be upgrades.
quarterly_data.figure: NAND less than 10% of wafer fab equipment spending

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced packaging: the mix of customer investment is changing, and Applied expects HBM and 3D chiplet stacking to be the fastest-growing packaging segments in 2026 - areas where Applied has very high share thanks to its materials deposition and removal technologies. Applied says it is #1 in advanced packaging overall and #1 in HBM, and packaging will be one of its highest-growth businesses this year and for the next several years (no size given on this call). CEO says customers want new packaging substrates as large as possible to connect more GPUs, memory and high-speed I/O at the highest density, with innovations in new substrates and new architectures ramping in the next few years, and expects Applied's packaging business to grow at a high compound annual growth rate for many years.
